Abstract: Molecular characterisation of sickle cell disease and classification of major haplotypes associated with the β-globin cluster (HBB gene) by means of SNP marker sequencing in a group of samples from Bolívar, Colombia.. BACKGROUND: Colombia has a mestizo population and the prevalence of haemoglobin variants varies according to each region, but heterozygous carriers can be found in all of them. AIM: To characterise sickle cell disease (SCD) haematologically, biochemically, and molecularly, and detect classic haplotypes by DNA sequencing in a group of samples from Bolívar, Colombia. SUBJECTS AND METHODS: Blood samples were collected after informed consent from volunteers from eight communities in the Bolívar department, plus samples from the Pacific region, Providencia Island, and Bogotá were included. data.title: Sickle cell allele HBB-rs334(T) is associated with decreased risk of childhood B
data.text: PMID 38009642: "Sickle cell allele HBB-rs334(T) is associated with decreased risk of childhood Burkitt lymphoma in East Africa." (Am J Hematol, 2024). Abstract: Sickle cell allele HBB-rs334(T) is associated with decreased risk of childhood Burkitt lymphoma in East Africa.. Burkitt lymphoma (BL) is an aggressive B-cell lymphoma that significantly contributes to childhood cancer burden in sub-Saharan Africa. Plasmodium falciparum, which causes malaria, is geographically associated with BL, but the evidence remains insufficient for causal inference. Inference could be strengthened by demonstrating that mendelian genes known to protect against malaria-such as the sickle cell trait variant, HBB-rs334(T)-also protect against BL. We investigated this hypothesis among 800 BL cases and 3845 controls in four East African countries using genome-scan data to detect polymorphisms in 22 genes known to affect malaria risk. We fit generalized linear mixed models to estimate odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CI), controlling for age, sex, country, and ancestry. The variant is a missense mutation, predicted to have a moderate impact by VEP. It is associated with drug interactions and is linked to decreased risk of childhood Burkitt lymphoma in some populations.
limitations: The evidence for the association with decreased risk of childhood Burkitt lymphoma is limited to a single study and may not be generalizable.

data.title: Grounded Interpretation
data.content:
The variant rs334 in the HBB gene is classified as Pathogenic in ClinVar, based on multiple submitters and no conflicts. The variant is a missense mutation, predicted to have a moderate impact by VEP. It is associated with drug interactions and is linked to decreased risk of childhood Burkitt lymphoma in some populations.

**Limitations:**
- The evidence for the association with decreased risk of childhood Burkitt lymphoma is limited to a single study and may not be generalizable.
